extracted.intended_audience: journalists, bloggers, media professionals, and general readers seeking American Cancer Society press releases
extracted.subtask_description: A listing/index of press releases (American Cancer Society) on a newswire, showing the metadata and surface content elements typically included in distributed press releases and the distribution platform UI cues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline / Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The press release includes a clear headline (title) summarizing the announcement (e.g., 'American Cancer Society Announces New Pediatric, Adolescent, and Young Adult Cancer Journal; Names Editor-in-Chief').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline should concisely state the main news or claim; examples on the page show full descriptive titles that name the organization and the action. Use a single line that captures the topic and main takeaway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date and time (with timezone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item is stamped with a release date and time and timezone (format shown: 'Apr 07, 2026, 10:00 ET').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the publication date and a time zone (ET on this page). This signals timeliness and can indicate embargo/release timing to journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead / Summary excerpt
rubrics_metrics.description: A short summary or lead sentence directly below the headline that previews the release (e.g., 'The American Cancer Society (ACS) today announced the launch of its fourth medical journal...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a one- to two-sentence lede that conveys the core information; listings show truncated previews ending with ellipses as the visible summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each release is clearly attributed to the issuing organization ('The American Cancer Society (ACS) today announced...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the issuing organization prominently in the lead or headline so readers immediately know the source and credibility of the news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language / Translated versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases may appear in multiple languages (examples: Spanish 'Nuevas investigaciones...', Chinese '新版ACS《癌症地图集》发布', and traditional/simplified Chinese variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide localized/translated headlines and summaries when applicable; list separate-language versions so non-English audiences can find the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: News topics / categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists news topics that categorize content (e.g., 'politics/government, business, technology, religion, sports/entertainment, science/nature, and health/lifestyle').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tag or categorize releases by topic so journalists and readers can filter by subject area; the page shows topic taxonomy at the top.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pagination and display controls
rubrics_metrics.description: UI controls for how many items are shown and sorting ('Items per page: 25 per page 50 per page 75 per page 100 per page' and sort option 'Latest'). Also: 'Making a selection with these dropdown will cause content on this page to change. News listings will update as each option is selected.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide filtering/sorting and items-per-page options on listing pages so users can navigate archives and find relevant releases; indicate that dropdown selections update the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience call-to-action / journalist services
rubrics_metrics.description: A dedicated callout for media professionals: 'Journalists and Bloggers — The news you need, when you need it. Join PR Newswire for Journalists' and 'Submit a free ProfNet request and find the sources you need.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit instructions and services for journalists (how to join, how to request subject-matter experts) so the release distribution supports news gathering and sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preview / excerpt formatting in listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings show a truncated excerpt of the release content (added ellipses indicate omitted text) to preview the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When showing releases in a list, include a short preview sentence or two to help readers decide which full releases to open; truncate with ellipses as needed.
